short: OVOL1 and OVOL2 are C2H2 zinc-finger repressors, the mammalian counterparts of Drosophila OVO/shavenbaby, that bind a short AT-flanked core, CCGTTA (equivalently TAACGG on the other strand). They act mainly as repressors of the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, holding epithelial cells in an epithelial state by shutting down ZEB1, ZEB2 and other EMT inducers, and OVOL1 additionally represses its own promoter and MYC. Mouse knockouts show defects in hair follicles, sperm, kidney, mammary ductal morphogenesis and epidermal progenitor arrest. In humans, a promoter point mutation that mis-expresses OVOL2 in corneal endothelium causes posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy type 1. OVOL1 and OVOL2 share one motif and cannot be separated from sequence.
long:
## The factors

The OVOL genes are the vertebrate orthologues of Drosophila ovo/shavenbaby (svb), a single locus whose
alternative transcripts supply two genetic functions: svb for the extracellular projections of epidermal
cells and ovo for female germ-cell survival. Humans have OVOL1 (11q13) and OVOL2 (20p11). A third gene,
OVOL3, is annotated in some species but has no measured motif in these databases and is not represented
here. The proteins carry four C2H2 zinc fingers, of which only about three contribute to specificity,
and they bind DNA as monomers. OVOL1 and OVOL2 are epithelial: skin and hair follicle, kidney, mammary
and corneal epithelium, placenta, and germ cells. Both act predominantly as transcriptional repressors;
OVOL1 represses by competing with the activator MYB at overlapping sites and by recruiting histone
deacetylase activity, and OVOL2 exists in repressor and non-repressor isoforms whose balance sets its
output.

## The motif

The consensus is CCGTTA, usually written with AT-rich flanks, and it appears in these databases in both
orientations: ACCGTTAT (JASPAR OVOL1 and OVOL2) and TAACGGT (HOCOMOCO OVOL2, and the atlas
representative). These are the same element read on opposite strands, so the apparent disagreement
between AT-rich and CG-containing renderings is only a strand convention. The information sits almost
entirely on the six-base core; the flanking A/T positions add affinity but little specificity, which is
why the shortest matrices here carry only about 6 bits.

The site was first defined by random-oligomer selection with the Drosophila OVO zinc-finger array, which
gave a statistically significant 9-bp consensus and showed that the recognition does not follow the usual
zinc-finger contact rules, consistent with the conclusion that some fingers in the array have degenerated
and no longer read bases. Mouse Ovol1 binding sites in genomic DNA converge on the same CCGTTA core, and
cross-species ChIP work in the Drosophila germline finds OVO at genomic CCGTTA motifs, so the core is
conserved from fly to mouse. The permissive hexamer CC/TGTTA is also reported, with high-affinity sites
favouring AT-rich flanks.

OVOL1 and OVOL2 are not distinguishable from sequence. Their matrices in all four databases converge
(family cohesion about 0.89, and the best cross-member similarities exceed 0.98), so a hit identifies the
family, not the member. One Vierstra archetype in this family, ACAGTTACA, is a variant with a different
third position and does not match the others closely; treat it as a separate, weakly supported model.

## Where it acts

OVOL sites are found in promoters and enhancers of epithelial-identity and EMT genes. Documented direct
targets include ZEB1 and other EMT inducers, MYC (repressed by OVOL1 in embryonic epidermal
progenitors), the OVOL1 promoter itself, and in flies the ovarian tumor (otu) promoter, where OVO binds
unusually close to the transcription start site. That proximity to start sites is a recurring feature:
OVO/OVOL sites cluster near TSSs rather than in distal enhancer deserts. In epithelial cells the factors
sit inside a double-negative feedback loop with ZEB1/ZEB2, so OVOL peaks tend to co-occur with ZEB and
SNAI motifs in the same regulatory regions, and with GRHL and KLF4 motifs that mark epithelial promoters.
The core is only 6 bp, so genomic occurrences are numerous in any sequence composition.

## Biology and disease

Mouse Ovol1 (movo1) knockouts are small, make aberrant hairs, show hypogenitalism with reduced fertility
and develop kidney abnormalities; the epidermal phenotype traces to failure of embryonic epidermal
progenitors to arrest and to de-repression of MYC. Ovol2 deletion blocks mammary ductal morphogenesis,
depletes stem and progenitor pools, and lets epithelial cells undergo EMT in vivo; conversely, forced
expression of the repressor isoform of OVOL2 reverts metastatic breast cancer cells toward an epithelial
state. OVOL1 and OVOL2 can both induce mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition in human cancer cell lines.
In human disease, posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy type 1 is caused by point mutations in the
OVOL2 promoter (c.-307T>C and related variants) that switch the gene on ectopically in corneal
endothelium, and OVOL2 maintains the corneal epithelial program by suppressing EMT. Reports in lung,
colorectal and breast cancer describe both tumour-suppressive and context-dependent pro-tumour effects,
and the literature here is not settled.

## Reading a hit

CCGTTA is six informative bases, so chance matches are frequent: expect many hits per megabase and treat
a single match as weak evidence. Sequence cannot distinguish OVOL1 from OVOL2, and in most epithelial
tissues both are expressed, so ChIP-seq in such a cell will not resolve them either. The evidence base
for this family is comparatively good: the HOCOMOCO OVOL1 and OVOL2 models carry in vitro support
(HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX), so "this protein binds this sequence" is well established even though
"this sequence was bound by this protein here" is not. Be alert to the reverse-complement rendering
TAACGGT, which is the same site and is easy to mistake for an unrelated motif. A match in an
EMT-associated promoter alongside ZEB or SNAI sites is more interpretable than an isolated hit, but the
direction of effect still has to come from expression or perturbation data.
caveats: The informative core is only 6 bp (CCGTTA / TAACGG), so chance matches are abundant and one hit is weak evidence. OVOL1 and OVOL2 share a single motif - cohesion here is about 0.89 with cross-member similarities above 0.98 - so a match identifies the family, not the member, and ChIP in epithelium cannot separate them either because both are usually expressed. The two strand renderings (ACCGTTAT and TAACGGT) are the same element and are often mistaken for different motifs. Evidence quality is good: the OVOL1 and OVOL2 HOCOMOCO models include in vitro HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX support. The Vierstra ACAGTTACA archetype is a poorly matching variant and should be treated separately.
